messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: covariates
parts:
Covariates in CFA can be at the factor level - that is they can predict the factor(s) - this is also called a MIMIC (multiple indicator multiple cause) model. 

A covariate can also exist at the item level. You might want to regress each item onto your covariates, to ensure that your factor that emerges is not just an artefact of some other variables. (For example, many variables are correlated with age in children: If you had a CFA with items like weight, height, math ability, number of friends, hours of computer use) you might find a factor, but that factor would just be age. In this case you can regression each item onto the covariate age, so you are essentially doing CFA on the partial correlations / covariances. (In some fields, it is common to residualize items on age, sex, sex^2 and sex*age before analyzing.)

Jeremy
